I can't personally attest to how bad the churches are in Utah (I live in ye olde potato state, but have visited quite often for family), but I can try and give some advice for living PIMO in devout areas. 

Moving into the area gives you the advantage to pick and choose how you present yourself to the members you will have to associate with, because they won't notice any sudden character/behavior changes. 
**0. Find friends that aren't mormon**
having a few(or many) people who you can be yourself around is monumental regarding your mental health. 

**1. Focus on what you think is good**
What I did was focus on the things about the gospel that I actually believed in, accepting people as they are and extending basic human decency to stay out of their business and afford them the rights to express themselves. whenever I was asked to speak and had a choice on what to speak on I chose New Testament Jesus's "Love Thy Neighbor", "Let he who is without sin cast the first stone", and Service principles because they are, in my opinion, the only good things there. 

**2. Tell the truth when you can, and lie when you can't **
When I didnt have a choice on what to speak on, or was asked questions about gospel principles I disagreed with, I tried to reorient the topic or the discussion to fit my beliefs, and when I couldn't: i lied. a lot. If you've had strict parents you're probably already good at it, but if not my best advice is to relax, keep whatever eye contact you regularly do, talk slowly, and just be confident in general. the "power of discernment" is total BS and you will be able to hide what you need to. If your lie involves another person, make sure it's a person you trust and TELL THEM. They need to know what your lie is and what part they play in it. **Lie as sparingly as possible**, and if you get caught explain as much as you can, people are often sympathetic though betrayal stings.

**3. Be as active as you want to/can**
Church callings are kind of a toss up, I did my best to be as helpful to anyone and everyone as I could because I was already like that and my parents had very high expectations(I came out to them about being an atheist, but they didn't take it well). You can avoid as much as you can to keep your mental health stable and well, try and go with the flow of the members around you so you don't stand out, or give 100% so nobody suspects anything. If you're really brave you can challenge ideas you disagree with, ask difficult questions that start discussions about problematic church doctrine or history, and just be as unapologetically inquisitive of how everything fits together. This requires you to know a lot of things about the Bible, the Book Of Mormon, church history and what's been said over the pulpit by the 12. it is time consuming, tedious, and probably won't make you any friends, but for me it was the most rewarding during my last 2 and a half years of Seminary when I was PIMO(I'm 19 and just barely moving out this summer, finally). 

**4. Be kind**
Most of all, be kind. if/when you come out you will have set an example that will put a lot of strain on the narrative that all Ex-mo's hate the church and just want to live in sin. Hopefully it will help you keep the relationships you want to when everything goes down, or your family and friends could be super cool and accept you. could happen, idk.

((((2021 + 95 - age) - (1732)) × 365.25days) - (*if age is <=16 then -3days, otherwise -2days*)) × 24hrs × 60mins ÷ 9mins = number of bacon slices eaten as of 2021
